item.title: Implication
item.description: In mathematical logic, implication is a logical operation typically denoted as P ⇒ Q, which can be read as "if P, then Q". It's a fundamental concept that forms the basis of many logical arguments and proofs. However, its definition often leads to confusion, particularly when the hypothesis is false.

item.title: Necessary and Sufficient Conditions
item.description: Oftentimes, there is considerable confusion when the concepts of necessary and sufficient conditions are taught. This article aims to make a clear exposition of these concepts from two points of view: that of set theory and logical implications.

item.title: The Uncountability of the Cantor Set: A Journey Through Base-3
item.description: The Cantor set is one of the most fascinating mathematical objects ever discovered. It's a set that seems to vanish before our eyes as we construct it, yet contains so many points that they cannot be counted - even using infinite counting! Today, we'll explore this remarkable set and prove its uncountability using Georg Cantor's famous diagonalization argument.
